title: The public door's events feed
description: What an organisation's own website reads from the portal's public door at events.json (/w/{name}/events.json on the portal's address, or /events.json on the organisation's public address): the organisation's events that somebody put on the public website, that are inside their website dates today, and that are still listed — not finished yet on their own clock; an event with no end time stays listed until the end of its day on its own clock, or for a fixed time after it starts when the organisation chose one (see listedUntil) — soonest first by the real moment each starts, so events on different clocks are in true order. Nothing members-only, draft, cancelled, postponed, deleted, unticked or another organisation's ever appears. Written by Portal\Core\PublicDoor::renderEvents() (web/_core/PublicDoor.php) and checked by tools/audit-checks/check_public_door_schema.py.
$comment: FOR MAINTAINERS. JSON has no comments, so every explanation lives here. A change to the shape is a change to what other people's websites read: add fields rather than rename or remove them, and raise `version` (and FORMAT_VERSION in PublicDoor.php) for anything a reader written against version 1 would misread. The check reads this file with a validator of its own that understands ONLY the keywords it lists in UNDERSTOOD, and fails on any other, so a keyword it cannot enforce can never sit here as decoration. Database numbers, who created or changed anything, contact details, map positions, capacity and registration are deliberately absent and must stay so (#493 plan, section 3).

format.description: Always the text webms-public-events, so a reader can tell this feed from the posters feed.

version.description: The version of this shape. 1 today.

generatedAt.description: The moment this answer was made, in UTC, as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. Browsers and caches may keep an answer for up to a minute.

events.description: The events, soonest first by the real moment each starts (startsAt), whatever clock each is on. At most the `limit` asked for (20 when none was asked, 50 at most). Empty when there are none.

organisation.description: The organisation the feed belongs to.

name.description: The organisation's name as the portal holds it.

timezone.description: The organisation's own time zone, an IANA name such as Europe/London. Each event carries its own zone as well, which may differ.

id.description: The event's short name in the portal's own addresses (its slug), which stays the same while the event exists. It is not the event's database number as a field, but a slug the portal made for itself can END in that number (to keep two slugs apart), so do not treat it as hiding one.

startsAt.description: When it starts, as an INSTANT: on the event's own clock, with that clock's offset from UTC, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+HH:MM. Use it to count down or compare; to SHOW a time use startsOnClock, which differs only inside the hour a clock skips. null only if the stored time could not be read.

endsAt.description: When it ends, in the same form, or null when it has no end time.

startsOnClock.description: When it starts, as the time written on the event's own clock, with NO offset: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS. SHOW this one (#493 P4b). It equals the reading in startsAt except on the morning a clock goes forward, when a time inside the missing hour stays as the organisation wrote it here while startsAt has to move past the gap. Use startsAt to count down or compare. null exactly when startsAt is null.

endsOnClock.description: When it ends, in the same form as startsOnClock, or null exactly when endsAt is null.

listedUntil.description: The moment the door stops listing this event, as an INSTANT in the same form as startsAt (#882). For an event with an end time it is endsAt. For an all-day event it is midnight at the end of its last day on its own clock. For an event with a start time and NO end time it is, by the organisation's choice, midnight at the end of its start's day on its own clock (the default) or exactly a fixed time after startsAt (15 minutes to 24 hours). It is when the door stops LISTING the event, NOT when the event ends: an event with no end time stays listed after it has begun, and nothing here says it is still happening. Use it to decide how long to keep an event on a list; a countdown or a "happening now" label should go by startsAt and endsAt, as the portal's own script does. null exactly when startsAt is null.

allDay.description: true when the event lasts the whole day, so its times are not meant to be shown.

timezone.description: The time zone the event's times are a clock reading in, an IANA name such as Europe/London.

detailsLimited.description: true when only the title, date and time may be shown publicly (an event copied in from an outside calendar under a rule that withholds its details). description and location are then null.

description.description: What the event is, as plain text the organisation wrote. null when there is none, or when detailsLimited is true. Show it as text, never as HTML.

location.description: Where it is, or null when nothing is recorded or detailsLimited is true. Never a telephone number, an e-mail address or a map position.

address.description: The place's postal address as text, or null.

url.description: The place's web page, only when it is an https:// address, else null.
